fusionDecisionAndVisibleImpact: The explanation now explicitly contrasts two questions: whether a proposed number satisfies an equation versus how to efficiently find an unknown solution. Substitution proves the former; trial-and-error alone is not presented as a general solving method.

Existing six original learner-visible sections retain their unit-specific sequence: contextual quantity model, formal one-variable/first-degree/equality criteria, candidate checking, misconception diagnosis, symbol-to-story read-back, and transfer/exit check.
